title: K-Means Clustering
subtitle: 3D Centroid Partitioning & Expectation-Maximization
summary: Partition unlabeled 3D point clouds into K spherical clusters by minimizing WCSS inertia.

evaluationChart.title: Elbow Method (WCSS / Inertia vs. K)
evaluationChart.description: Identifies the optimal K at the 'elbow' where marginal inertia reduction sharply flattens.

advantages: Fast, scalable O(T · n · K · d) convergence on large datasets.
Simple geometric interpretation with explicit cluster centroids.
Works effectively on compact, well-separated spherical clusters.
limitations: Requires specifying K in advance and is sensitive to centroid initialization.
Fails on non-convex, crescent, or varying-density clusters.
Sensitive to outliers that pull cluster means away from dense cores.
applications: Anchor box generation in object detection

formulas.label: Cluster Assignment (E-Step)
formulas.description: Assigns each 3D point to its nearest centroid.

formulas.label: Centroid Update (M-Step)
formulas.description: Moves each centroid to the arithmetic mean of its assigned points.

formulas.label: Inertia (WCSS Objective)
formulas.description: Total within-cluster sum of squared distances.

codeTemplates.fromScratch:
import numpy as np

def kmeans(X, k=3, max_iters=10):
    centroids = X[:k].copy()
    for _ in range(max_iters):
        dists = np.linalg.norm(X[:, None, :] - centroids[None, :, :], axis=2)
        labels = np.argmin(dists, axis=1)
        centroids = np.array([X[labels == j].mean(axis=0) for j in range(k)])
    return centroids, labels
codeTemplates.scikitLearn:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
import numpy as np

X = np.random.randn(120, 3)
km = KMeans(n_clusters=3, init='k-means++', random_state=42).fit(X)
print('Inertia:', km.inertia_)
